This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 (2) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred feeling aggrieved by award dated 22nd of December, 2007 in Motor Vehicles Case No.660/2005 by Eighth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur (M.P.) whereby claim filed under Section 166 of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal has been rejected on the ground that the Tribunal has no jurisdiction to adjudicate the application.

entities.text: Eighth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Facts in brief are that the appellant filed an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for compensation regarding motor vehicle accident dated 06th of March, 2005.
Place of incident was mentioned as in front of Maharaja Transport, Rink Talkies Parasiya, Police Station-Parasiya, District- Chhindwara (M.P.).

Appellant mentioned his address as Nai Basti, Police Station-Gohalpur, District Jabalpur and address of respondent no.1 was mentioned as Balaji Ward No.2 Chandrapur, Police Station-City Kotwali, District-Chandrapur (M.H.) and address of Prabhu Dayal vs Sachin Buradkar on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82834320/

1 respondent no.2 was mentioned as Revenue Colony (Ram Nagar) Post and Tahsil Police Station-Chandrapur, District-Chandrapur (M.H) and the address of respondent no.3 was mentioned as National Insurance Company Limited Jabalpur.

3. Tribunal in paragraph no.9 of the award has concluded that the appellant is not the resident of Jabalpur and in paragraph no.13 has concluded that the office of respondent no.3 National Insurance Company is situated at Jabalpur but this alone does not confer the jurisdiction to Tribunal at Jabalpur.
He also referred to Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.
4. Feeling aggrieved by this award, appeal has been preferred assailing the finding of the Tribunal regarding jurisdiction.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent no.3 also does not support the finding of the Tribunal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

Section 166(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 confer the jurisdiction to adjudicate the application of the Claims Tribunal having jurisdiction over the area within the local limits which the accident occurred, or to the Claims Tribunal within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the claimant resides or carries on business or within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the defendant resides.

8. Undisputedly, the office of respondent no.3 is situated at Jabalpur and that office is a division office so the finding of Tribunal regarding want of jurisdiction is against Section 166 (2) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
9. Hence, this appeal is allowed and the award dated 22.12.2007 is set aside and the matter be remanded back to the Tribunal to decide the application on priority basis.
10. As both the parties are present before this Court so they are directed to remain present before the Tribunal on 19th of February, 2024.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE julie Prabhu Dayal vs Sachin Buradkar on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82834320/
